paper.title: Charon: A Unified and Fine-Grained Simulator for Large-Scale LLM Training and Inference
paper.authors: Mengtian Yang, Zhekun Zhang, Mingheng Wu, Jianwen Yan, Hanshi Sun, Li-Wen Chang
paper.license: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/); figures reproduced as a style reference with attribution, copyright stays with the authors

how_to_read: open figures/<id>/print.png (print size) or preview.png (detail) and manifest.json; star = must-see. These show one paper's house style; borrow its look, not its layouts.

templates.why_chosen: Charon-style teaser: left half is the system as a stacked platform card fed by framework logos, right half two boxed result cards (cost, accuracy) that carry the claim in numbers.
templates.what_to_learn: Say the contribution three times in one column: a red 'old way' arrow versus a green 'with us' label over the same input/output, a grey platform card holding three full-width pastel capability bars, and two black-framed side cards with one number each in the same red/green.

templates.why_chosen: A whole background section in one tall single-column figure: three black-framed bands (a)-(c), each split by a dash-dot rule into a diagram and its companion (zoomed block, parallelism catalogue, motivation chart).
templates.what_to_learn: Frame each panel with one thick black rectangle and a bold (a)/(b)/(c) in its top-left corner, split a panel with a dash-dot vertical rule, and keep one fill per concept across panels (blue = transformer block / forward, pink = backward / K / layer, peach = output / V, mint = norm / expected).

templates.why_chosen: Panel (a) zooms one Transformer block of a grey/blue layer stack into a pale-blue detail box with two converging guide lines.
templates.what_to_learn: Draw the zoom as two straight lines from the selected stack box to the corners of a tinted detail box; inside it, rotated tall bars (Norm Layer) act as section dividers.

templates.why_chosen: The canonical Charon-style overview: inputs on the left, the platform as one big rounded frame with three equal subsystem boxes, outputs on the right, the whole thing inside a thick black outer frame.
templates.what_to_learn: Title each flank and each subsystem with bold text, put the subsystem name at the bottom of its box, open each subsystem with a grey header bar, and fill only the leaves with the role colours (blue / peach / mint / pink); tiny glyphs (node-link graphs, timeline bars, a pruned tree) stand in for what each stage produces.

templates.why_chosen: Two stacked panels separated by a dash-dot rule: (a) a tracing pipeline from a native model to forward / backward graphs, (b) three tinted dotted pass groups between two rotated grey bookend bars.
templates.what_to_learn: Use rotated grey bars as the input and output bookends of a pass pipeline, give each pass family a pale dotted region (peach / blue / pink) holding white rounded steps with vertical ellipses, and draw graphs as pastel node-link glyphs coloured by direction (blue forward, pink backward).

templates.why_chosen: Panel (b) is a left-to-right pipeline of three pass groups whose steps run top-down inside each group.
templates.what_to_learn: Hand off between groups with an elbow arrow from the last step of one group to the first of the next.

templates.why_chosen: Each engine is a full-height tinted panel in its identity colour (blue / peach sharing one panel, mint, grey), and the fused engine on the right re-uses the same three colours as its decision boxes.
templates.what_to_learn: Tint the whole panel, not just a header, with the subsystem's identity colour, put white boxes inside, and let a later decision flow refer back to each subsystem by a dotted box in that same tint; Y / N labels on the branches.

groups.why_chosen: Before/after on the same time axis with worked bandwidth values: (a) every communication op at full speed, (b) the same ops slowed down where they overlap, with the bandwidth arithmetic written beside the rows.
groups.what_to_learn: Encode the link by hue (green NVLink, blue IB) and the state by fill strength plus outline (solid saturated = full speed, pale dotted = slowed down), give the legend as two arrow-pairs above the axis, and write the congestion arithmetic in the link's own colour next to the rows it explains.

groups.why_chosen: Per-rank operator timelines without and with dynamic SP, coloured by request (blue shades = request 1, red = request 2), ending in a dashed deadline line and a 'Saved Time' double arrow.
groups.what_to_learn: Colour the work by whom it belongs to, not by operator; split a bar's fill when one operator serves two requests; mark the gain as a dashed vertical finish line plus a labelled double-headed arrow.

groups.why_chosen: Panel (a) explains zigzag attention as KV chunk strips and causal-mask triangles per rank, with circled chunk numbers and a shade ramp.
groups.what_to_learn: Number chunks with circled digits and give each chunk one step of a single-hue shade ramp so the reader can follow it from the strip into the mask cells.
